lead: there is an hour before the house is up, and a door, and nothing behind it has ever been witnessed. twenty years of things have come out of that room and nobody has watched one of them being made.
sun: the making happens out of sight, which was never decided; it is simply where your hands work. a thing gets thought of, built and finished behind a shut door, and what leaves the room leaves detached, on its way to somebody who will run it under their own name. the two halves that could corroborate each other never meet: the process had no witness, and the product carries no author.
moon: cover here is real and it rests on one point of contact — the hour, the shut door, your continuing to get up for it. nothing in you offers a tour. so the people nearest you assemble a reserved interior with something valuable kept in it, and what is actually under there is a bench, a light, and whatever is currently half-built and will be gone by friday.
pull: nobody has watched you make anything. what came out of that room is running in other people's lives, and the only place that could vouch for it has never held a second person.
tension: what gets said, eventually, by someone who has lived beside you for years, is that they do not know you. it is accurate, and it has nothing to do with disclosure — you answer every question put to you. the room takes one occupant by construction, and the thing you would have to let them watch is the one thing you have never done in company: something going wrong at the bench for two hours before it goes right.
cost: behind a shut door, with nobody to perform for, a thing can be tried eleven ways in a morning and abandoned without a word said about it, which is why so much has come out of that room. the same door means the only account of your life that includes the work is one you would have to give yourself, and you have never taken minutes.

lead: who is told what, how money gets decided, what happens when somebody is ill: all of it was begun by you inside four years, and nobody living there thinks of it as begun.
sun: everywhere else your starts leave and keep going. this one has an inside, so the same rate of making runs on into a space that does not release anything: a shelf where a shelf was needed, a rule about sundays, a different arrangement for the year the money was bad. each of them worked, each got absorbed within a month, and the household holds no date for any of it.
moon: an enclosure is the made thing with a person inside it, and being inside is what stops it being visible. from a chair in that kitchen the arrangements are conditions, weather, the given. your children will describe their upbringing later without one sentence in it about design, and you will not supply the sentence either. standing inside a thing is the one position from which it cannot be pointed at.
pull: of everything you started, the household is the only one that stayed, and staying put it where you cannot look at it. the people in it call it how things are.
tension: nothing else in your life has a lid on it. the rate that other places absorbed and forgot arrives entirely at this address — the kitchen reorganised, the routine revised, the order of who does what rebuilt because you saw the flaw. at the table it comes out as never leaving anything alone, and you agree, and by the spring something else has been rebuilt. making is how you attend to people in a room.
cost: four people are inside something that stands by its own construction, and it will still stand when you are dead. you are inside it too. every other thing your hands started went out where distance could report whether it was any good; this one has never been seen from outside, so nothing reports, and you will die without a view of it.

lead: fourteen stations of road lie between your sun and your moon, the widest gap this circle has, and it shows as two talents that never meet: you start what you cannot follow, and you finish what you did not begin.
sun: the pushing end of you works at the start of things and leaves immediately. somebody is stuck, an hour later something exists that was not there — the phrase, the introduction, the first concrete piece — and it goes on without you inside the week, under their name, uncounted. that end of your life is hundreds of beginnings whose outcomes have never reached you.
moon: the other end does the opposite work: you take a person the whole way, at your own inconvenience, through the part where they would have stopped, and you leave them at the boundary of what they were going to. that end has arrivals in it, dozens, each one witnessed. what it has never had is anything you started. the two ends have no shared case.
pull: two hundred people got started by you and never seen again; forty got walked the whole way and remember your face. the road between those two facts is as wide as this circle goes.
tension: people arrive asking for one thing and receive whichever end of you the situation reached first. the one who needed company for a year gets a first move and a name to ring and is on their own by tuesday; the one who needed a shove gets walked to an edge they had not asked to reach. the two capacities never confer, so nothing chooses, and the person who got the wrong one does not come and tell you.
cost: almost nobody does either of these, and you do both: a start that costs the other person nothing to accept, and a crossing where you stay until the far side is reached. neither leaves you anywhere. the near end keeps no record and the far end is a country you turn round at, so a lifetime of it has produced no place where you are known to have been.

lead: you were twenty-three when you got the first one going, and there has not been a season since without one — no place in the run where one stretch of your life ends and another starts.
sun: each thing you started came loose and went on without you, which is the ordinary arrangement, and it means none of them is what continues. what continues is the reaching: the same motion at twenty-three and at sixty-one, aimed at whoever was in the room, with no interval anywhere in which your hands were not partway into something. from your side there are no separate episodes at all.
moon: a line only does its work while both ends pull, and yours is held from one. every start let go of the other end by design — that is what made them survive — so the length drawn taut here runs from your first year of it to this week, through forty years of other people's lives, fastened at the far end to nothing that pulls.
pull: forty years of it is one pull with no knot in it, and every person who felt it felt a few months of something that has never let up.
tension: a household, a trade and about nine people have arranged themselves around the assumption that the next thing will start, because forty years of them have. the winter you were ill, nothing fell over — what you started had never been leaning on you — and nothing came the other way either. a length under load from one side is still under load. the people holding the other ends have no idea there is a line.
cost: something begun thirty years ago can be picked up this afternoon at the same tension it was left at, no re-entry, no explaining where you have been, because you never went anywhere. a run with no divisions has nowhere in it to stop. there is no completed portion to hand anybody, and whoever arrives in your life at sixty arrives partway along and stays partway along.
